Make a symmetric key

Source: R/keys.R
jose_key_oct.Rd

jose_key_oct() wraps a secret as a JSON Web Key of type oct (RFC 7518 section 6.4), the key type of the HS*, A*KW, A*GCMKW and dir algorithms.

Usage

jose_key_oct(secret, alg = NULL, kid = NULL, use = NULL, key_ops = NULL)

Arguments

secret

The key, as a raw vector of at least one byte.

alg

The one algorithm the key is meant for, such as "HS256", or NULL. When set, a token whose alg differs is refused.

kid

A key identifier, or NULL. See jose_with_kid().

use

"sig" or "enc", or NULL.

key_ops

The operations the key may be used for, from "sign", "verify", "encrypt", "decrypt", "wrapKey", "unwrapKey", "deriveKey" and "deriveBits", or NULL.

Value

A jose_key.

Details

The secret is a raw vector, never a string: a key is bytes, and a password is not a key. Secrets live in ordinary R memory, which R can copy and cannot reliably wipe; keep long-lived secrets out of saved workspaces.

See also

as_jose_key() to read a JWK, jose_jwk() to write one.

Examples

key <- jose_key_oct(as.raw(1:32), alg = "HS256", kid = "k1")
key
#> <jose_key> oct, 256 bits
#>   kid "k1"
#>   alg HS256
#>   private: yes (not shown)
